finding: _VALID_VARIANTS is a static readonly array used only to validate the variant property — but the variant property is already typed as a literal union, making runtime validation a redundant layer that will never catch TypeScript-level mistakes and will silently diverge from the type if either is updated.
recommendation: Remove _VALID_VARIANTS and the validation block in updated(). The literal union type on `variant` is the authoritative constraint; runtime clamping belongs in FormMixin patterns or user-facing inputs, not typed properties.

finding: The inline event comment block at lines 196–199 (`/** Dispatched when the button is clicked. @event hx-click */`) is dead JSDoc — it lives inside a private method body where no tooling reads it. The event is already documented on the class JSDoc at line 24.
recommendation: Delete the inline JSDoc comment block at lines 196–199. The class-level @fires tag is the correct location.

finding: Section header comments (`// ─── Form Association ───`, `// ─── Public Properties ───`, etc.) are visual noise that duplicate what TypeScript visibility and property grouping already communicates. They provide zero information beyond what the next line of code says.
recommendation: Remove all ASCII-art section divider comments. If logical grouping is needed, a single blank line suffices. The code is readable without them.

finding: _renderSpinner() and _renderInner() are private render helpers that each produce a TemplateResult — but _renderSpinner() is only ever called from _renderInner(), and _renderInner() is only called from render(). Three-level render call chain for a spinner SVG is architectural overhead with no reuse justification.
recommendation: Inline _renderSpinner() into _renderInner() and inline _renderInner() into render(). Two fewer function calls per render cycle, zero loss of clarity.

finding: rgba() fallback values are used throughout hx-button.styles.ts (e.g., `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)` at line 206, `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7)` at line 217). Modern CSS color syntax uses `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.5)`. These fallbacks are token fallbacks, but they use legacy four-argument syntax.
recommendation: Replace all `rgba(r, g, b, a)` fallbacks with `rgb(r g b / a)` modern syntax throughout the stylesheet.

finding: The inverted mode comment `/* Primary inverted — slight transparent white overlay on hover */` at line 210 describes what the code does (set a lighter background color), not why. The word 'inverted' in the selector already tells you the context.
recommendation: Delete the comment. The selector `:host([inverted]) .button--primary:hover` is self-documenting.

finding: The `hx-change` event is registered in HTMLElementEventMap with a union type `CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>`. The text input never dispatches an event with `checked` in its detail — that shape belongs to hx-checkbox and hx-switch. This pollutes the global event type registry with incorrect type information.
recommendation: Change the HTMLElementEventMap registration for hx-text-input's `hx-change` to `CustomEvent<{ value: string }>` only. The `checked` branch is a copy-paste error.

finding: The `WcTextInput` deprecated type alias is defined at line 523 but is NOT exported from the package index. It is dead code — it cannot be used by consumers and will never trigger the deprecation path.
recommendation: Either export `WcTextInput` from the index with `export type { WcTextInput }` to complete the deprecation migration path, or delete the alias entirely if migration is complete.

finding: Five private slot-tracking handlers (_handleLabelSlotChange, _handleErrorSlotChange, _handlePrefixSlotChange, _handleSuffixSlotChange, _handleHelpTextSlotChange) are structurally identical — each reads `slot.assignedElements().length > 0` and assigns to a different `@state` field. This is mechanical duplication that creates maintenance risk.
recommendation: Extract a private `_trackSlot(e: Event, target: '_hasLabelSlot' | '_hasErrorSlot' ...)` helper, or use a single generic slot handler that reads a data attribute from the slot element to determine which state field to update.

finding: The help-text render path at lines 487-503 contains two identical `<div part='help-text'>` blocks — one for `_hasHelpTextSlot` and one for `this.helpText && !hasError`. Both render the exact same template. This is structural duplication that inflates the render output size.
recommendation: Merge the two conditions: `const showHelp = this._hasHelpTextSlot || (this.helpText && !hasError)` and render the block once.

finding: The `_handleInput` method at line 341 calls `this._internals.setFormValue(this.value)` immediately after assignment, and `updated()` at line 254 also calls `this._internals.setFormValue(this.value)` on value change. The form value is being set twice per keystroke.
recommendation: Remove the `this._internals.setFormValue(this.value)` call from `_handleInput`. The `updated()` lifecycle hook is the correct single place to sync form value with Lit property changes.

finding: The `hx-change` event in `HTMLElementEventMap` at line 760 uses the same union type `CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>` as text-input. hx-select never dispatches a `checked` field. This is a copy-paste contamination of the global event type system.
recommendation: Change the HTMLElementEventMap registration to `CustomEvent<{ value: string }>` — the exact shape dispatched by `_dispatchChange()` at line 543.

finding: connectedCallback() at line 218 calls super.connectedCallback() and nothing else. This is an empty override — Lit does not require override of connectedCallback if there is no additional logic.
recommendation: Delete the entire connectedCallback() override. The comment directly above disconnectedCallback explains the real logic lives there.

finding: The `form`, `validationMessage`, and `validity` getters (lines 260-278) are not marked `override` but shadow identical getters that almost certainly exist on HelixElement/ElementInternals. If the base class defines these, missing `override` is silent API divergence. If the base class does not define them, they are new public API without JSDoc.
recommendation: Add `override` keyword if they shadow base class getters. If they are new API additions, verify JSDoc exists — `/** Returns the associated form element, if any. */` is the only docstring present and it is on the wrong getter for `form`.

finding: The hidden native `<select>` element at render line 710 has `aria-hidden='true'` set but also receives `aria-label`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, and `aria-required` attributes. ARIA attributes on aria-hidden elements are ignored by all AT and constitute dead markup that engineers will misread as functional.
recommendation: Remove all ARIA attributes (aria-label, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, aria-required) from the native select element. It is presentation-only; the custom combobox element carries all ARIA semantics.

finding: HTML comments in the render template (`<!-- Label -->`, `<!-- Select Wrapper: trigger + listbox -->`, `<!-- Custom Trigger -->`, `<!-- Custom Listbox Panel -->`, `<!-- Hidden slot -->`, `<!-- Error -->`, `<!-- Help Text -->`) are informational noise that document what each element is, which the element's CSS class and part attribute already state.
recommendation: Delete all HTML comments from the render() template. The markup is readable without them.

finding: The `_WcSelect` deprecated export at line 766 uses `export type { HelixSelect as WcSelect }` — this aliases the class itself, not a dedicated type. Consumers importing `WcSelect` get the full class constructor type, which breaks tree-shaking tooling that can't distinguish it from a value export.
recommendation: Use `export type WcSelect = HelixSelect` inside the file and `export type { WcSelect }` from the index, consistently with other deprecated aliases in the codebase.

finding: The dual-comment pattern on private fields throughout hx-dialog — e.g., `/** Cached focusable elements... */\n/** @internal */` at lines 113-115, and `/** Guards against rapid open/close... */\n/** @internal */` at lines 117-119 — splits one logical comment block across two JSDoc blocks. JSDoc parsers will only use the last block attached to the declaration.
recommendation: Merge into a single JSDoc block per field: `/** @internal Cached focusable elements — populated on open, cleared on close. */`. Eliminate the split pattern across the entire file.

finding: _openDialog() dispatches `hx-open` BEFORE `void this.updateComplete.then(...)` resolves, meaning the event fires before focus has been set. Consumers who listen for `hx-open` to then programmatically focus an element will conflict with the component's own focus logic running afterwards.
recommendation: Move `this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('hx-open', ...))` to inside the `updateComplete.then()` callback, after `_cachedFocusableElements[0]?.focus()`. Events should fire after the component is fully ready.

finding: The `_renderHeader()` private method (line 542) has no explicit return type annotation. Private render helpers that can return `TemplateResult` or `typeof nothing` must have their return type declared explicitly for maintainability.
recommendation: Annotate: `private _renderHeader(): TemplateResult`. Same applies to `_renderFooter()`, `_renderNonModalBackdrop()`, and `_renderDescription()`.

finding: The inline arrow function in render() `@click=${() => this.close()}` at line 557 creates a new function reference on every render call. This defeats Lit's dirty-check optimization for event listeners and causes the listener to be removed and re-added unnecessarily.
recommendation: Extract to a named private method `private _handleCloseClick = (): void => { this.close(); }` and reference it in the template as `@click=${this._handleCloseClick}`.

finding: modal defaults to `true` at line 153. A boolean HTML attribute with a default of `true` violates HTML boolean attribute semantics — attribute presence means true, absence means false. Setting `modal` as default-true means `<hx-dialog>` without any attributes is already modal, but `<hx-dialog modal>` is indistinguishable from the default. The attribute cannot be meaningfully toggled off via HTML.
recommendation: Default `modal` to `false` and require consumers to add `modal` attribute explicitly. Or rename to `non-modal` with default `false` to preserve the more common case being accessible by default.

finding: closeOnBackdrop uses a custom converter (fromAttribute: `value !== 'false'`) making it default to `true` via the same HTML boolean attribute anti-pattern. Additionally, the `toAttribute` stringifies booleans, causing the attribute to always be present on the host element, which is non-standard behavior for boolean attributes.
recommendation: Use standard boolean attribute behavior: `closeOnBackdrop = false` default, presence of attribute enables it. Or document the non-standard converter behavior explicitly in the JSDoc with a warning.

finding: The `_handleClick()` method at line 241 is a one-line wrapper that calls `_toggle()` with no additional logic. It is a function used exactly once that adds a call-stack layer with zero justification.
recommendation: Remove `_handleClick()` and reference `_toggle` directly in the template: `@click=${this._toggle}`. Ensure `_toggle` is bound correctly (it already uses standard method syntax, not an arrow, so binding via `.bind(this)` or converting to an arrow field is required).

finding: The dual-comment pattern on private fields — `/** Reference to the native button... * @internal\n   */` at line 193 — has a stray space before the closing `*/` and splits the @internal tag onto a separate line. This is a malformed JSDoc comment that will confuse CEM generation.
recommendation: Fix to a single properly-formed JSDoc: `/** @internal Reference to the native button element acting as the switch track. */`

finding: The `hx-change` event in HTMLElementEventMap at line 350 uses the union type `CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>`. hx-switch always dispatches `{ checked: boolean; value: string }`. The `{ value: string }` branch is incorrect and will mislead consumers who destructure the event detail.
recommendation: Change the HTMLElementEventMap registration to `CustomEvent<{ checked: boolean; value: string }>` — the precise shape dispatched by `_toggle()`.

finding: The `updated()` lifecycle hook at line 229 casts `changedProperties` to `Map<PropertyKey, unknown>` to call `.has('_activePanel')` — a private state field. This is an architectural mistake: Lit's `PropertyValues<this>` does not surface `@state()` properties in changedProperties because state fields are not declared as properties via `@property()`. The `.has('_activePanel')` check will never be true, making `_updateTabsAndPanels()` unreachable from this path.
recommendation: Remove the `updated()` override for `_activePanel` detection. Instead, call `this._updateTabsAndPanels()` directly inside the `this._activePanel = ...` assignment in `_activateTab()`, which is the correct reactive pattern.

finding: The tablist aria-label falls back to the string literal `'Tabs'` at render line 479 when `this.label` is empty. A fallback of `'Tabs'` is a non-descriptive accessible name that provides no information about what the tabs represent — WCAG 4.1.2 requires meaningful labeling.
recommendation: Remove the `|| 'Tabs'` fallback. If `label` is empty, either render nothing (let devWarn() in firstUpdated() surface the problem) or render `aria-label=${this.label || nothing}` so the absence is explicit and detectable by axe-core.

finding: The `_warnInvalidSlotContent()` method (lines 355-380) uses `this.shadowRoot?.querySelector<HTMLSlotElement>()` inside a slot change handler. The slot references are stable after first render; querying the shadow DOM repeatedly on every slot change is wasteful. The component already has the slot in the render tree.
recommendation: Use `@query` decorators to cache references to both slot elements, then access them directly in `_warnInvalidSlotContent()`.

finding: The actionsSlotChangeHandler and titleSlotChangeHandler are stored as nullable function references on instance fields (lines 135-137), manually added and removed in firstUpdated/disconnectedCallback. This is a manual event listener management pattern inside a component that should use Lit's declarative `@slotchange` binding in the template.
recommendation: Replace the manual addEventListener/removeEventListener lifecycle with `@slotchange=${this._handleActionsSlotChange}` directly in the render template, and convert the handlers to named private methods. Delete the handler reference fields entirely.

finding: open defaults to `false` but the component is described as 'add the `open` attribute to show the alert' — a boolean attribute with false default. This is correct. However, `dismissible` defaults to `false` and the close button is only rendered when `dismissible` is true, yet the `hx-close` event documentation says 'Dispatched when the user dismisses the alert' — consumers can also programmatically set `open = false` without `dismissible`. The event therefore fires in non-dismissible mode on programmatic close, but the JSDoc implies user-only origin.
recommendation: Clarify the @fires JSDoc: `hx-close - Dispatched when the alert is hidden, either via the dismiss button or programmatically.` Also dispatch `hx-close` from `updated()` when `open` transitions false, not only from `_handleDismiss()`.

finding: The CSS class concatenation `alert__title ${this._hasTitle ? 'alert__title--visible' : ''}` at line 391 uses string interpolation inside a template literal rather than `classMap`. This is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which uses `classMap` for conditional CSS classes, and bypasses Lit's optimization.
recommendation: Replace with classMap: `class=${classMap({ 'alert__title': true, 'alert__title--visible': this._hasTitle })}`. Same issue at line 397 for `alert__actions`.

finding: The nested Promise.resolve().then() chain at lines 236-248 uses two microtask ticks to clear and re-inject announcer text. The justification comment is valid, but the double Promise.resolve pattern produces non-obvious async flow that is difficult to test reliably. The inner promise is also not awaited or returned.
recommendation: Replace with `queueMicrotask(() => { announcer.textContent = ''; queueMicrotask(() => { announcer.textContent = text; }); })` to make the two-tick intent explicit and idiomatic.

finding: The `hx-change` event in HTMLElementEventMap at line 407 uses union type `CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>`. hx-checkbox always dispatches `{ checked: boolean; value: string }`. The `{ value: string }` branch is incorrect type information in the global event registry.
recommendation: Change to `CustomEvent<{ checked: boolean; value: string }>` — the exact shape dispatched at line 255.

finding: The comment `// P2-05: monotonic counter — collision-free, deterministic, SSR-safe` appears twice (line 12 and line 281), and similar P-numbered comments appear throughout the file. These are internal ticket/audit references that mean nothing to engineers reading the code cold. They are wasted bytes in a production source file.
recommendation: Delete all P-numbered internal reference comments. If the behavior needs explanation, the explanation itself (not the ticket number) belongs in the comment.

finding: The `_handleKeyDown` method (line 264) calls `e.stopPropagation()` on Space key events. Stopping propagation on keyboard events inside a web component is a global side-effect that breaks consumers who listen for Space keydowns on parent elements for legitimate reasons (e.g., closing a popover on Space).
recommendation: Remove `e.stopPropagation()`. Only `e.preventDefault()` is needed to suppress the native browser scroll behavior. Event propagation should not be halted.

finding: The `_toastEl` query field uses non-null assertion syntax (`@query('.toast') private _toastEl!: HTMLElement | null`) at line 82. The `!` non-null assertion is in direct contradiction with the explicit `| null` union type on the same field. This is logically incoherent — either the field can be null (remove `!`) or it cannot (remove `| null`).
recommendation: Remove the `!` non-null assertion. The field type should be `HTMLElement | null` without the assertion, consistent with how it is used (null-guarded at lines 201-203).

finding: The `_emitHide()` method at line 193 hardcodes a 300ms fallback setTimeout for `hx-after-hide`. This magic number is not referenced to any design token or CSS variable — it is an arbitrary duration that will silently become wrong if the CSS transition duration changes.
recommendation: Extract to a named constant `private static readonly _HIDE_TRANSITION_FALLBACK_MS = 300` with a comment explaining it mirrors the CSS transition duration, or read it from the computed style.

finding: The `show()` and `hide()` public methods (lines 132-143) contain redundant guard checks: `if (!this.open) { this.open = true; }` and `if (this.open) { this.open = false; }`. Setting a Lit property to its current value does not trigger a re-render, so these guards are functionally equivalent to unconditional assignment and add no value.
recommendation: Simplify to `show(): void { this.open = true; }` and `hide(): void { this.open = false; }`. Lit's property system handles the dirty-check.

finding: The ToastVariant type alias is exported from hx-toast.ts and re-exported from the index, but the `variant` property type on HelixToast at line 49 is written as an inline literal union `'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info'` rather than using the exported `ToastVariant` type. The type and the property definition are not connected, making them silently divergeable.
recommendation: Type the variant property as `variant: ToastVariant = 'default'` to enforce the single source of truth.

finding: The `_cardId` and `_headingId` fields (lines 120-125) have verbose JSDoc comments explaining they are unique identifiers and their purpose in ARIA attributes. This is exactly what the field name and usage already communicate. The comments add no information.
recommendation: Remove the JSDoc blocks on `_cardId` and `_headingId`. Replace with `/** @internal */` only if CEM suppression is needed.

finding: The `_dispatchCardClick()` method (line 183) has an inline JSDoc comment at lines 186-190 (`/** Dispatched when an interactive card is clicked... @event hx-click */`) inside the method body. As with hx-button, this is dead JSDoc — tooling cannot parse it from inside a method. The event is already documented at the class level line 24.
recommendation: Delete the inline JSDoc comment block. The class-level @fires annotation is canonical.

finding: The `@state()` JSDoc comments on `_hasImage`, `_hasHeading`, `_hasFooter`, `_hasActions`, and `_headingText` (lines 86-114) all contain verbose sentences like 'Tracks whether any content is assigned to the image slot, controlling slot container visibility.' These describe what the field is — not why it exists or any non-obvious behavior. They are over-documented.
recommendation: Replace verbose JSDoc on internal state fields with `/** @internal */` only. The field name makes the purpose obvious.

finding: The `_lightDomDescription` element is appended as a child of `this` (the host element) via `this.appendChild()` at line 171. This injects a `<span>` into the consumer's light DOM — a side effect that will corrupt the consumer's DOM structure, break CSS child selectors, and appear unexpectedly in `querySelector` results on the parent. Web components must not modify their own light DOM children.
recommendation: Append the description element to `document.body` instead (with `position:absolute; clip:...` visually-hidden styling) and remove it in `disconnectedCallback`. This keeps the host's light DOM clean while maintaining the aria-describedby cross-shadow reference.

finding: All four `@query` fields (_defaultSlot, _contentSlot, _triggerWrapper, _tooltipEl, _arrowEl) at lines 102-110 use the non-null assertion operator (`!`). These elements are conditionally present in the render tree and can be null during SSR, before first render, or if the template changes. The `!` assertions on query results will produce runtime errors if these methods are called before render completes.
recommendation: Remove all `!` non-null assertions from `@query` fields. Declare them as `HTMLElement | null` and add null guards at call sites, consistent with how `_dialogEl` is handled in hx-dialog.

finding: The `--hx-tooltip-z-index` CSS custom property at line 14 in hx-tooltip.styles.ts has a hardcoded fallback of `9999`. Magic z-index values without a documented scale are an anti-pattern — this value will conflict with any consumer who has z-index layers above 9999 and has no connection to the `--hx-z-index-tooltip` token fallback already in the var() chain.
recommendation: Remove the `9999` raw fallback. Use only `var(--hx-tooltip-z-index, var(--hx-z-index-tooltip))` and ensure the token is defined in the token layer with a documented value on the z-index scale.

finding: The `_applyCollapse()` method at line 222 uses `document.createElement('hx-breadcrumb-item')` to imperatively create a DOM element and inject it into the consumer's light DOM (line 253: `firstItem.after(this._ellipsisItem)`). This is a pattern that directly mutates the consumer's authored markup and will cause double-rendering, break server-side rendering, and violate the expectation that light DOM belongs to the consumer.
recommendation: Render the ellipsis element entirely in the shadow DOM using Lit's reactive state. Track `_isCollapsed` and `_collapsedItemCount` as `@state()` fields and render the ellipsis button in the shadow template alongside the slotted `<ol>`.

finding: The `_handleEllipsisKeydown` method at line 276 manually handles Enter and Space keyboard events on the dynamically-created ellipsis button. The ellipsis element is a `<button>` — native buttons already handle Enter and Space natively. This manual handling is redundant, adds complexity, and will interfere with the native behavior.
recommendation: Remove `_handleEllipsisKeydown` and the `this.addEventListener('keydown', this._boundEllipsisKeydown)` registration. The native button element handles keyboard activation.

finding: The `_getAnimationDuration()` method at line 399 returns a hardcoded `300` milliseconds as the animation duration. This value must match the CSS transition duration but has no connection to it — it is a magic number that will silently become wrong whenever the CSS transition is changed.
recommendation: Remove the hardcoded return value. Either read the actual computed transition duration from the panel element via `getComputedStyle` + `parseFloat`, or export the duration as a CSS custom property token (`--hx-drawer-transition-duration`) that both the CSS and this method reference.

finding: The `_hideBackgroundFromScreenReaders` method (line 408) walks the parent chain and then iterates all `document.body.children` to apply `aria-hidden` to siblings. Applying `aria-hidden` to arbitrary sibling elements is a fragile pattern that will conflict with consumer-managed `aria-hidden` state and breaks if the drawer is not a direct child of body.
recommendation: Use the `inert` attribute on sibling elements instead of aria-hidden — it is more reliable, composable with existing aria-hidden states, and standard for this use case. Or use a native dialog element which handles this via the modal stack automatically.

finding: The inline arrow functions in _renderHeader() — `@click=${() => { this.open = false; }}` at lines 600 and 627 — create new function references on every render. This is the same per-render allocation anti-pattern as hx-dialog.
recommendation: Extract to a named bound method `private _handleCloseClick = (): void => { this.open = false; }` and reference it in both template locations.

finding: The `_parseInput` method at line 401 has the condition `if (raw === '' || raw === null)` where `raw` is typed as `string`. The `raw === null` check is dead code — a `string` type cannot be `null` in TypeScript strict mode. This is either a stale JavaScript-era guard or a sign the function was typed incorrectly.
recommendation: Remove the `|| raw === null` branch. The function signature is `(raw: string)` — null is not a valid input. If null inputs are possible, type the parameter as `string | null`.

finding: The `_applyStep()` method at line 430 dispatches `hx-change` directly (not `hx-input`), even when triggered by stepper button presses which are not 'change on blur' events. This conflates the semantics of `hx-change` (value committed after interaction) with `hx-input` (value changing during interaction).
recommendation: Stepper button increments should dispatch `hx-input` not `hx-change`. Dispatch `hx-change` only when the native input fires its own `change` event (on blur after modification).

finding: The `declare private _input: HTMLInputElement | null` syntax with `declare` keyword at line 189 is non-standard for Lit's `@query` decorator pattern. The standard pattern is `@query('.field__input') private _input: HTMLInputElement | null | undefined`. The `declare` keyword here may indicate a TypeScript declaration emit artifact being used incorrectly in source.
recommendation: Remove `declare` and use the standard `@query('.field__input') private _input: HTMLInputElement | null | undefined` declaration.

finding: The `size` property type `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | (string & Record<never, never>)` at line 61 is an intentional widening trick to preserve autocomplete while accepting arbitrary strings. This technique is valid but produces a confusing public API — the type appears to accept any string but the JSDoc only documents the token values. New engineers will not understand why the type is written this way.
recommendation: Add an explicit JSDoc note in the @attr tag: `@attr hx-size - Token values 'sm'|'md'|'lg' or any CSS size string. The type uses a string-widening pattern to preserve IDE autocomplete for token values.`

finding: The `_isTokenSize()` private method at line 101 is a type predicate used to determine whether to apply a custom style or not. It is called exactly once inside `render()`. A type predicate used once in a render method with a three-condition OR check can be inlined directly into the render expression without loss of clarity.
recommendation: Inline: `const customSizeStyle = !['sm','md','lg'].includes(this.size) && this.size ? styleMap({...}) : styleMap({})`. Delete `_isTokenSize()`.

finding: The `_SEMANTIC_VARIANT_LABELS` static field at line 172 uses `Partial<Record<HelixBadge['variant'], string>>` — a perfectly valid type. However, the type is derived from the class itself (`HelixBadge['variant']`), creating a self-referential dependency that prevents the constant from being extracted to a module-level const without importing the class. A `BadgeVariant` type alias would eliminate this coupling.
recommendation: Extract `export type BadgeVariant = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'neutral' | 'info'` and use it for both the property type and the labels map: `Partial<Record<BadgeVariant, string>>`.

finding: The `WcBadge` deprecated type alias has a JSDoc `@since 0.1.0` and `@removal-target 1.0.0` at lines 244-248. The package is currently at version 0.1.0 which means `@removal-target 1.0.0` is actively in the removal window. Deprecated aliases that should have been removed are shipping in 3.0.0.
recommendation: If WcBadge is past its removal target, remove it now before 3.0.0 ships. If the target needs to be extended, update the JSDoc. Do not ship code with a past removal target date.

finding: The `style='display:none;'` inline style on the hidden slot at render line 731 is an inline style applied to shadow DOM content. This bypasses the component's own CSS stylesheet, mixes inline and class-based styling, and cannot be overridden by consumer CSS. It is also inconsistent with every other invisible slot pattern in the codebase which uses `hidden` attribute or CSS classes.
recommendation: Add `.slot--hidden { display: none; }` to hx-select.styles.ts and use a class attribute instead of an inline style.

finding: The hx-date-picker.styles.ts file is a single minified CSS string with no line breaks — the entire stylesheet is one continuous line. This is not a build artifact but appears to be source code that has been minified and checked in. It is impossible to review, diff, or maintain.
recommendation: Expand the stylesheet to properly formatted CSS with consistent indentation, one declaration per line, and logical section groupings. Minification belongs in the build pipeline, not in source files.

finding: The hx-date-picker.styles.ts minified stylesheet contains `rgba(0, 0, 0, .1)` and `rgba(0, 0, 0, .1)` as raw color values inside box-shadow fallbacks that are not behind design token variables. These are hardcoded color values that do not adapt to theme changes, dark mode, or forced-colors.
recommendation: Replace raw `rgba()` shadow fallback values with semantic token references: `var(--hx-shadow-sm)` or similar. If the shadow tokens are not yet defined, define them.

finding: The hx-select.styles.ts line 194 has `rgba(13, 17, 23, 0.12)` as a raw fallback value inside a token var() chain. Raw hardcoded RGBA color values inside production component stylesheets are a zero-tolerance violation of the design token architecture.
recommendation: The fallback must reference a defined token or be removed. Either define `--hx-overlay-neutral-12` with a proper value in the token layer, or use an existing shadow token.

finding: The test 'renders with shadow DOM' (hx-button.test.ts:13) asserts `expect(el.shadowRoot).toBeTruthy()`. This test will pass whether or not shadow DOM rendering is functional — `shadowRoot` is truthy the moment the custom element is defined with a shadow root option, even if render() throws or produces nothing.
recommendation: Change to `expect(shadowQuery(el, 'button')).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLButtonElement)` which actually verifies the render output exists inside the shadow DOM.

finding: The test 'exposes "button" CSS part' (hx-button.test.ts:18) asserts `expect(btn).toBeTruthy()`. This is a truthy-only assertion — it does not verify the element has the part attribute or is the correct element type. It will pass for any non-null element.
recommendation: Change to `expect(btn).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLButtonElement)` and `expect(btn?.getAttribute('part')).toContain('button')`.

finding: The test 'dispatches hx-click on click' (hx-button.test.ts:300) asserts `expect(event).toBeTruthy()` as its only meaningful assertion after receiving the event. The test verifies the event fires (via oneEvent timeout behavior) but does not assert anything about the event.
recommendation: Add meaningful assertions: `expect(event.type).toBe('hx-click')`, `expect(event.bubbles).toBe(true)`, `expect(event.composed).toBe(true)`. The existing test only proves the event loop did not time out.

finding: hx-dialog does not use a native `<dialog>` element's inherent modality — it wraps the `<dialog>` in a custom open/close state management layer while also calling `dialog.showModal()`. The dual state management (component `open` property + native dialog open state) creates a synchronization risk where the native dialog can be in a different open state than the component property, particularly during rapid open/close cycles guarded by `_isTransitioning`.
recommendation: This is an architectural issue requiring a full design review. At minimum, add an integration test that cycles open/close rapidly 10 times and asserts the final state is consistent between `this.open`, `this._dialogEl.open`, and the `aria-modal` attribute.

finding: The package index.ts exports `resetIdCounter` from the base infrastructure (line 21). A function named `resetIdCounter` that resets stable, SSR-compatible ID generation should not be part of the public API — calling it at runtime after components have mounted would create duplicate IDs, breaking ARIA associations in any live components on the page.
recommendation: Remove `resetIdCounter` from the public index export. If it is needed for test isolation, export it from a separate test utilities entry point only.

finding: The index.ts exports `HelixAuditController` (line 29) as a public library export. An audit controller is an internal observability tool — exposing it publicly means consumers will import it, creating a tight coupling between internal telemetry infrastructure and the public API surface.
recommendation: Move `HelixAuditController` and its associated types to a separate entry point (`@helixui/library/controllers`) that is explicitly marked as unstable, or remove it from the public bundle entirely.

finding: Multiple `Wc*` deprecated type aliases are re-exported from the index (WcBadge, WcContainer, WcDivider, WcNav, WcSwitch, WcTag, WcTheme, WcTreeView, WcTreeItem) without a consistent deprecation timeline or migration guide. The barrel exports include both `Hx*` and `Wc*` aliases for the same types, doubling the exported type surface.
recommendation: Establish a single 3.0.0 cutoff: all `Wc*` aliases must be removed in this release since 3.0.0 is a major version. If they are not being removed, they need an explicit `@deprecated since 0.x.0, will be removed in 4.0.0` tag with a breaking change entry in the changeset.

finding: The DRAWER_SIZE_MAP constant at line 16 maps preset strings to rem/percentage values. The `sm: '20rem'`, `md: '30rem'`, `lg: '40rem'` values are hardcoded pixel equivalents that do not reference design tokens. These sizing values should derive from the token system.
recommendation: Replace raw rem values with design token references: `sm: 'var(--hx-drawer-size-sm, 20rem)'` etc. This allows the token layer to control default sizes without requiring component code changes.

finding: The cssprop documentation for hx-tabs at lines 29-45 mixes token references with raw hardcoded fallback values inline (e.g., `var(--hx-color-neutral-200, #e9ecef)`, `var(--hx-color-primary-600, #1d4ed8)`). These raw hex fallbacks in JSDoc cssprop declarations are published to the Custom Elements Manifest and become part of the documented API, normalizing raw color values instead of tokens.
recommendation: Remove the raw hex fallbacks from JSDoc @cssprop declarations. Document only the token variable name: `@cssprop [--hx-tabs-border-color=var(--hx-color-neutral-200)]`. The hex fallbacks belong in the CSS token definition layer, not in component documentation.
